html: The Kalaamaya are an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland south of Western Australia, in the country around Southern Cross between the wheatbelt and the Goldfields. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their language, also spelt Karlamay, is poorly recorded but seems close to Noongar; the speech of the Nyaki-nyaki has been counted as a dialect of either. As of 2015 a single fluent speaker remained. Other neighbours were the Ballardong to the west, the Badimaya to the northwest and the Wangkatha to the east. Gold found at Southern Cross in 1888 brought the first miners into the area.
